audit_decisions.ink: The p descender, tall l, short u and final s are identifiable through the strike. The detached point is to the right of its endpoint. The apparent word left of MD-graphes belongs to the slanted marginal baseline, not the body sentence. The raised word begins with the looped descending g and reduced accented vowels; it has no initial sp sequence. The stroke under catégorie ends with two converging short strokes forming a right-pointed end. A separate comma follows the word; a plain underline drops its terminal geometry. The cancelled glyph is heavily hatched, so MD is recorded as an alternative only. The live symbol has a closed upper bowl and a long closed lower loop, unlike the open upper bowl of the separate marginal capital G. The word has a tall initial t and low o-u-s continuation; there is no initial closed d bowl supporting donc. The marginal capital is separate from the body g, and line-break commands do not alter its text. The short e-n-s sequence ends in a distinct point; the terminal stroke is not a separate v shape. On the rotated marginal crop a descending p and tall l are followed by an x-like crossing and short terminal strokes. Classes lacks the descender; a distinct t-i sequence for complexités is not secure. Overlap still prevents a definitive full reading. The exposed beginning contains the large descending g, short accented vowels and a tall medial t-like stroke. The ending meets the body formula; groupes is not established. The last word has open c, low a and a short s ending, without a tall t. Two detached points precede the adjacent outlined body glyph; a third cannot be separated.
